children: Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures fell on Tuesday as traders continue to monitor if the meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping this week could spur more Chinese buying of American supplies. Wheat fell and corn was unchanged.
The most-traded soybeans on the Chicago Board of Trade
fell 0.2% to $13.25-1/4 a bushel by 0258 GMT. CBOT wheat
dropped 0.3% at $7.24-1/5 a bushel, while corn

* Traders hope Beijing may remove a 10% import duty on US soybeans, encouraging private Chinese buyers to resume purchases. Market participants focused on the Thursday meeting because China is the world's biggest soybean importer.
* US Treasury chief Scott Bessent said he had successful talks with the Chinese on trade issues over the weekend.
* Rain has delayed autumn US harvests in some areas of the Midwest, slowing the flow of fresh crops into the supply pipeline, analysts said.

* In major grain producing Black Sea regioin, the largest Ukrainian drone attack reported so far on the Moscow region killed three people and damaged an oil refinery, while an overnight Russian attack on the Kyiv region killed four people, authorities said on Sunday.

* Russian companies have been re-purposing fertilizer, coal, and other cargo terminals at Russia's Baltic and Arctic ports to handle grain exports after Ukrainian drone attacks disrupted shipments through the Black Sea, five sources said.
* Both Russia, the world's largest wheat exporter, and Ukraine saw a drastic reduction in grain exports due to tit-for-tat attacks on vessels and ports in the Black Sea over recent months.
* In the previous export season, almost 90% of Russia's seaborne grain exports were shipped through the Black Sea.
Oil prices gained on Tuesday as the market steadied after several days of declines, with investors awaiting developments on potential US-Iran talks at the United Nations General Assembly this week.
